# testdata

Fixture rc files used by the unit tests (`go test ./...`), the pty smoke test (`just smoke`) and manual exploration (`just try`). Nothing here is real user data.

Everything under `testdata/` is ignored by `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` package matching, so this directory costs nothing in normal builds.

## Quick use

```sh
just try testdata/bashrc                  # open the TUI on a fixture (bash)
just try testdata/zshrc zsh               # zsh
just try testdata/config.fish fish        # fish
just try testdata/large/bashrc            # 2000 aliases: scrolling and wrapping
just smoke                                # run every fixture through the real binary
just smoke edge                           # only paths containing "edge"
just fixtures                             # regenerate testdata/large (deterministic)
just fixtures 20000 7                     # 20k aliases, seed 7 (stress test, don't commit)
```

`try` and `smoke` copy the fixture into a throwaway `$HOME`, so your real rc files are never read. Fixture file names are matched to a shell by name (`*zshrc*` → zsh, `*fish*` → fish, otherwise bash).

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `bashrc`, `zshrc`, `config.fish` | Hand-written, realistic, diverse. Every `alias` line must parse. |
| `large/` | Generated by `gen/main.go`: 2000 aliases per shell with comments, blank lines, exports and functions mixed in. |
| `edge/` | One small file per bug or tricky input (see below). |
| `empty/` | Files with zero aliases (empty-state handling). |
| `minimal/` | Exactly one alias per shell. |
| `sourced/` | A rc file that sources other alias files, for the multi-file feature. |
| `gen/` | The deterministic generator for `large/`. |

## Regular fixtures

| File | `alias` lines | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| `bashrc` | 168 | Navigation, listing, git, docker/k8s, system, packages, dev tools. `ll` is defined twice (so 167 distinct names). Also contains pipes, `&&`, `;`, `$(…)`, backticks, env-var prefixes, escaped `\$`, `=` inside values, emoji, CJK, a 400-character command, a bare unquoted value, and `unalias`/function noise. |
| `zshrc` | 157 | oh-my-zsh style noise (`setopt`, `bindkey`, `zstyle`, `autoload`), modern-CLI replacements, fzf pipelines, cloud tools, unicode. Contains one quoted alias name (`alias 'open'=…`), which the parser resolves to `open`. |
| `config.fish` | 103 | Mixes `alias name 'cmd'` and `alias name='cmd'`, plus `abbr`, functions and an `if status is-interactive` block (no aliases inside it). The `abbr` lines are **not** aliases. |

## Large fixtures (`large/`)

| File | Aliases | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| `large/bashrc` | 2000 | unique names, ~65 lines with non-ASCII, ~165 `&&` chains, ~90 env-var prefixes, ~24 lines over 200 chars |
| `large/zshrc` | 2000 | same generator, zsh noise lines |
| `large/config.fish` | 2000 | half the lines use the space-separated form |

- The first line of each file is a header, `# pa-fixture: shell=<sh> aliases=<n> seed=<s>`, so a test can read the expected row count.
- Output is **deterministic**: the same `-n` / `-seed` always produces byte-identical files (checked). Only the default (`-n 2000 -seed 1`) is meant to be committed.
- They contain only plain, well-formed definitions, so they are a scroll / wrap / performance test. Tricky inputs are in `edge/`.

## Edge cases (`edge/`)

"Valid rows" is how many rows a correct parser shows. Every row below is asserted in `internal/alias/parse_test.go` (`TestEdgeFixtures`), and `internal/app` runs every file through the whole program. "Was" is what the pre-rewrite parser did, kept for history.

| File | Issue | Valid rows | Was |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `short-a-lines.bashrc` | #3 | 2 | crash |
| `alias-without-value.bashrc` | #4 | 2 | crash |
| `alias-without-value.zshrc` | #4 | 1 | crash |
| `alias-without-value.config.fish` | #4 | 1 | crash |
| `multiple-per-line.bashrc` | #8 | 6 | 3 mangled rows |
| `indented.bashrc` | #9, #1 | 7 | only 1 shown |
| `indented.config.fish` | #9 | 4 | only 1 shown |
| `flags.zshrc` | #10 | 11 | names like `-g L`, `-s txt` (`{jpg,png}` is one name; brace expansion is not modelled) |
| `flags.config.fish` | #10 | 4 | names included `--save` |
| `quotes-escapes.bashrc` | #11 | 17 | wrong quote/escape handling. 20 alias lines, 3 intentionally invalid (unterminated quote, lone quote, `a = b`), which must be skipped without crashing. Each alias has an `# expect:` comment above it. |
| `trailing-comments.bashrc` | #12 | 7 | `# comment` leaked into the command (it is now in `Alias.Comment`) |
| `duplicates.bashrc` | (#40) | 7 lines / 3 names | all kept; the shell's "last wins" is a future diagnostic |
| `special-names.bashrc` | #10 (`--`) | 25 | `-- -` shown with the `--` |
| `fish-separators.config.fish` | #8/#11 | 18 | exercises `=` vs space, `a=b` inside values, empty values, tab after name |
| `crlf.bashrc` | none | 4 | worked |
| `bom.bashrc` | none | 2 | **first alias silently dropped** |
| `no-trailing-newline.bashrc` | none | 2 | worked |
| `unicode-wide.bashrc` | (#15/#30) | 16 | CJK, emoji, ZWJ, RTL, combining marks, full-width, box drawing; check alignment by eye |
| `very-long-command.bashrc` | (#15/#30) | 6 | 200-char name, 500-word command, 3000-char unbroken word |
| `ansi-escapes.bashrc` | none | 4 | raw `ESC[…m` and BEL inside commands; now shown as `␛` / `␇` symbols |
| `bad-bytes.bashrc` | none | 4 | invalid UTF-8 (shown as `�`). The tab in `alias tab<TAB>here=…` splits the word, so that line defines `here`, as in a real shell. |

Notes:
- When you add a fixture, add its row here **and** an entry in `TestEdgeFixtures`.
- `just smoke` only checks that the binary neither crashes nor hangs; the unit tests check correctness.

## Empty and minimal

| File | Aliases | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| `empty/bashrc`, `empty/zshrc`, `empty/config.fish` | 0 | Plenty of other content, plus **commented-out** `# alias …` lines that must not count |
| `empty/zero-bytes.bashrc` | 0 | 0-byte file |
| `empty/blank-lines.bashrc` | 0 | only newlines |
| `minimal/*` | 1 | one alias each (`ll`) |

All five empty files make the program print `pretty-alias: no aliases found in <path>` to stderr and exit 0.

## Multi-file (`sourced/`)

For #2 / #31. Copy the whole directory's files into a fake `$HOME` to test source-following.

| File | Role | Aliases |
|---|---|---:|
| `bashrc` | entry point; sources `~/.bash_aliases`, `~/.config/aliases/work.sh`, a missing file, an absolute missing path, and `self-include.sh` | 1 |
| `bash_aliases` | the Debian/Ubuntu default; includes the long `alert` alias | 5 |
| `work.sh` | sourced via `$HOME/.config/aliases/work.sh` | 3 |
| `self-include.sh` | sources itself and `work.sh` (recursion guard test) | 1 |
| `zshrc` → `zsh_aliases` | zsh equivalent; also a `for … source` glob | 1 + 2 (`zsh_aliases` has an `alias -g`) |
| `config.fish` → `conf.d/aliases.fish` | fish auto-loads `conf.d/*.fish` | 1 + 1 (+ one `abbr`) |

Once following `source` is implemented (#31), `bashrc` should yield `from_bashrc` + 5 from `bash_aliases` + 3 from `work.sh` + `from_self_include` (once) = **10** distinct rows, and missing files must not crash. Today only the entry point itself is read, so 1 alias is shown; the tests assert that.

## Adding a fixture

1. Put it in the right folder, named `<what-it-tests>.<rcname>` (for example `foo.bashrc`) so `try` / `smoke` can infer the shell.
2. Add a row to the table above (valid rows, issue, today).
3. For byte-level cases (CRLF, BOM, control characters) generate the file with `printf` rather than an editor, which may "fix" it.
4. `go test ./...` and `just smoke`.
